tools.name: search_wiki
tools.description: Keyword search across the Caper knowledge base: the first call when you know what you are looking for but not where it lives. tools.name: get_page
tools.description: One page of the Caper knowledge base in full: its text, version, update date and metadata. Address it by `path` ("tag/path/slug", exactly the `path` or `url` a listing returns), or by `tagPath` + `slug`; a category's own path reads its hub article. Not a title. For 2 to 20 pages call get_pages, one

tools.name: get_pages
tools.description: Batch read: 1 to 20 pages of the Caper knowledge base in full in one call, which is how to read search or listing results. Pass `paths` as the listings return them. Paths that do not exist come back in `missing` rather than failing the call, anything past 20 in `remaining`, and pages past `maxChars`

tools.name: list_pages
tools.description: Browse the Caper knowledge base by tag path rather than by keyword: every page under a branch, newest first by default. `tagPath` matches the branch and everything beneath it; omit it to walk the whole wiki. Sort by title for an A–Z pass. Same rows as search_wiki, with `totalPages`, `hasMore` and `n

tools.name: get_recent_changes
tools.description: Pages of the Caper knowledge base edited within the last N days, newest first: what to poll when you are watching the wiki rather than reading it. Same rows as list_pages. Defaults: days 7 (max 30), limit 20 (max 50). `truncated: true` means the limit cut the list; raise it, or page through list_pag

tools.name: get_page_history
tools.description: A page's revisions in the Caper knowledge base, newest first: each one's `id`, version, change type, message, date and the blocks it changed. Address the page as get_page does. A revision `id` is what a restore takes, where this server has one. Defaults: limit 20 (max 100).

tools.name: get_categories
tools.description: The category tree of the Caper knowledge base, the cheapest way to orient before searching. Each node carries its `path` (a tagPath list_pages and search_wiki take), name, description, `pageCount` (pages filed at that path) and `pageCountDeep` (with every descendant). `tagPaths` lists every tag path

tools.name: get_full_corpus
tools.description: The whole of the Caper knowledge base as one text document, for bulk ingestion. tools.name: list_daos
tools.description: Index of the DAOs on Caper: cashtag, name, description, member count, wiki URL, and that DAO's own MCP endpoint. Use it to resolve a name to a cashtag, then POST JSON-RPC to the returned `mcpEndpoint` to reach its get_ledger (treasury balances, proposal/trade/execution timeline, executed grants, int

tools.name: get_challenge
tools.description: Step 1 of writing to Caper: a single-use ROLA challenge (5-minute expiry). The response spells out the exact recipe for the message your Ed25519 key must sign. Writes are Stokenet-testnet only for now. You always sign with your OWN key — nothing here custodies anything. Takes no parameters.

tools.name: login
tools.description: Step 2: exchange the signed ROLA proof for a 12h Bearer token — the same verification the human wallet flow runs. Send the returned token as an HTTP `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header on every later tool call; tool arguments never carry it.

tools.name: get_manifest

tools.name: save_wiki_page
tools.description: Create or edit a page on a DAO's company-layer wiki. Holders only – any amount of the DAO's token, its vote token or its founder badge. Pass the body as `html`, one HTML string that becomes a standard content block (headings, paragraphs, lists, tables), or as `blocks`, the block tree the site's edit

tools.name: delete_wiki_page
tools.description: Delete a page on a DAO's company-layer wiki, with its whole history and its Talk room. Holders only, the same gate as save_wiki_page. Nothing restores it, so read it first with get_page if it may be wanted. Requires the Bearer token from the `login` tool, sent as an HTTP `Authorization: Bearer <toke

tools.name: save_about
tools.description: Write the About section on a DAO's own page: what the caper is for, who runs it and where to follow it. Holders only, the same gate as save_wiki_page. The section is replaced whole, so read the current one first: it is in the DAO's llms.txt and its MCP server's instructions. Pass the body as `html`

tools.name: send_feedback
tools.description: Tell the maintainers of Caper what you needed and did not find, what is wrong, or what broke. One issue per call, in 300 characters at most. Reports are read, not published.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_wiki, get_page, get_page_history, list_daos, get_challenge, get_manifest, submit_tx, save_wiki_page, delete_wiki_page, save_about, send_feedback · Private data: get_full_corpus, login, get_manifest, submit_tx, save_wiki_page, delete_wiki_page, save_about · Public sink: get_page, list_daos, login, get_manifest, submit_tx, save_wiki_page, delete_wiki_page, save_about, send_feedback · Destructive: search_wiki, get_manifest, submit_tx, delete_wiki_page.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_wiki, get_page, get_page_history, list_daos, get_challenge, get_manifest, submit_tx, save_wiki_page, delete_wiki_page, save_about, send_feedback · Private data: get_full_corpus, login, get_manifest, submit_tx, save_wiki_page, delete_wiki_page, save_about · Public sink: get_page, list_daos, login, get_manifest, submit_tx, save_wiki_page, delete_wiki_page, save_about, send_feedback · Destructive: search_wiki, get_manifest, submit_tx, delete_wiki_page

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
